The hydrogen mass fraction of 14.28% corresponds to a hydrocarbon with formula \(C_nH_{2n}\). Since \(Z\) is saturated, does not react further with hydrogen, and is a common solvent, \(Z\) is cyclohexane, \(C_6H_{12}\).

The disproportionation fitting the data is:

\[
\text{cyclohexene } (C_6H_{10}) + \text{1,4-cyclohexadiene } (C_6H_8)
\rightarrow \text{cyclohexane } (C_6H_{12}) + \text{benzene } (C_6H_6)
\]

Mixture \(X\) therefore contains \(C_6H_{10}\) and \(C_6H_8\), whose hydrogen atoms total:

\[
10 + 8 = 18
\]

Answer: D
